reportAccuracyNotes: FIX143's controls are labelled backwards, and the correction strengthens the finding rather than weakening it. FIX143 reports 'Positive control in the same bytes: annotations-on vs hidden reads 17,203 and 18,453 added at the two button rects; negative control 0/0.' VF44 measures 17203 and 18453 as the annotations-on-minus-hidden delta on the COURT'S SOURCE, where the pushbuttons are still live widgets. In the pre-repair DELIVERED bytes the same comparison reads 16840 and 17985 with annotations on and the IDENTICAL 16840 and 17985 with -hide-annotations, i.e. 0 added -- which FIX143 recorded as its 'negative control 0/0'. That zero is not a negative control at all: it is the proof that the caption had been flattened into page content and would print whether or not a viewer draws annotations. The numbers are real and the conclusion is right; the attribution of which artifact each came from is wrong.

FIX143's 'Page 1 removes the same 35,656 pixels of button chrome' is the SOURCE's live widget chrome (17203 + 18453 = 35656), which appears as 'removed' only when the baseline is the source rendered WITH annotations. What the repair actually withdrew from the delivered page is 34825 px per page (2374864 -> 2340039 dark px on page 1, and 651690 -> 616865 on page 2). Both numbers are traceable; they are not the same quantity.

laneFindings.advisoriesAreAWriteOnlyChannel: CONFIRMED, with the code that proves it. The eight advisories were there: FIX143's parent commit carries all eight in the family's build-findings.json, four per fixture, check 'flattening_materialised_the_forms_own_widget_caption', each with drawnText 'Print Form' or 'Reset Form', each rect, and each with the note 'a filed copy carries the words at the foot of the sheet. Recorded for visual review.' FIX143's commit removes all eight, correctly: the condition is gone, and a VF44 rebuild reproduces the file without them. Nothing read them. The only factory consumer of the file, readBlockingBuildFindings in scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/generate-proven-family-legal-delta.mjs line 98, reads `.blocking ?? []` and nothing else; grep across scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/ and scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/ finds no consumer of the advisory array at all. ANSWERED PLAINLY: a builder that finds a defect and files an advisory nobody reads is WORSE than one that does not find it, not merely equal to it. Equal would be a system that stayed silent and stayed honestly ignorant. This one produced a durable written record that the packet stamps 'Print Form' on a court filing, printed PASS_COMPLETE beside it, and shipped for months -- so the artifact that should have stopped the packet became the evidence that everyone had been told and nobody acted. It converts a detection failure into a disclosure failure, and it means the next reviewer who finds this defect can be told, truthfully and uselessly, that it was already known.

printFormChromeElsewhere.thePopulationNumber: detachNestedControlFields defaults to FALSE in the shared finalizer (scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs line 649). Across the whole repository 13 scripts pass it true, of which 7 are census-v1 family builders: al-misd-nonconviction-90-set, az_marijuana_expungement_arrest_no_charges-set, ca-1203-4-set, ct-cleanslate-petition-set, md_10105_early-set, ne-setaside-custodial-set, rcap-in-custom-pleading. There are 311 census-v1 builder scripts and 193 --official-pdf-fill family directories. So roughly 186 official-PDF-fill families are built without the flag that stops a nested pushbutton caption reaching the filing. That is not 186 defects -- most source forms carry no pushbutton, and a non-nested pushbutton is caught by the flat sweep -- but it is the bounded population a sweep has to cover, and the safeguard is an opt-in that six families out of nearly two hundred have taken.
